title: Social Network Connections
short_description: Analyze friendship networks to compute degrees of separation, discover isolated social communities, and serve bounded friend recommendations.
real_world_context: Modern social networking platforms maintain massive friendship graphs connecting hundreds of millions of user profiles. To deliver features like friend recommendations ('People You May Know'), mutual connection distance badges ('2nd-degree connection'), and community partitioning for viral content propagation, backend graph engines perform high-speed breadth-first searches, connected component analysis, and bounded graph traversals with strict latency budgets.
learning_objectives: Model large-scale social networks as unweighted bidirectional graphs.
Compute shortest path degrees of separation between users using Breadth-First Search (BFS).
Identify independent social clusters and evaluate community sizes using Depth-First Search (DFS).
Implement Depth-Limited Search to generate bounded friend recommendations within latency constraints.
Manipulate singly linked lists to audit and reverse relationship timeline logs.
